title: Dead Local Variables (The Leftover Assignment)
pattern: Declaring and initializing local variables that are never read or evaluated thereafter.
why_bad: Increases visual noise and confuses readers, who must figure out whether the variable was intended to be used or represents a bug.
detection: Local variable declarations whose identifiers do not appear as expressions in any downstream path.
counterexample: Context-dependent (usually flagged by compilers; but LLMs can identify variables kept alive solely to bypass compiler warnings).
fix: Delete the variable declaration and its initialization expression.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 24 ("Routine-Level Refactorings"), p. 186; Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3.
